doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Grammars of improvisation and boundaries
summary: Many ways to learn to improvise are symbol systems; grammar is a box and freedom needs boundaries.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well that’s again, the thought that there’s a syllabus and an answer and an exam where ultimately you look at the piano keyboard, it’s just one big chord. There’s no wrong note

it’s just one big pool of possibility. And you know the interesting thing is there are so many ways to learn how to improvise, there really are. I mean you can learn it from the feet up or the head down. You can learn to do it through the harmonics. You can do it through the melody. You can do it through modes. You can do it — there’s so many ways to learn how to improvise. It makes you realize that these are all symbol systems. These are all grammars. There’s the harmonic grammar. There’s a melodic grammar. Whatever appeals to you, depending on your nature, is probably how you’ll approach it. And it’s a very personal experience and there’s no right fit for everybody, but basically it’s a conversation. And the grammar that you use determines what you get to say just like there are some things you can’t say in English but you can say five different ways in Spanish. Or you know the grammar that you use is part of the box you’re in and you’re trying to get out of. You’re trying to push the boundaries. And as we all know there’s no freedom without boundaries, because there’s no definition of freedom without the lack of freedom. So I think the — I’m totally confused.
All right. I was just going to say, when we — we will be transcribing this and you’re very quotable, Ben.
